newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel strengthens against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel strengthens against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel representative rate was fixed higher against the dollar on Thursday following the weakening of the U.S. currency on overseas markets, dealers said.

"Activity rose slightly today because the business sector was converting foreign currency (into shekels) for mid-month tax payments. The dollar declined abroad and this led to the shekel's rise," said a dealer at Israel Discount Bank.
"The Bank of Israel had to intervene again in the market buying dollars to support the basket. I believe that it purchased less than $100 million," the dealer said.
The central bank has been intervening regularly in the market to defend the currency basket rate, which has been trading at the bottom end of its band for two months.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3650 shekels against 3.3730 on Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6507 shekels against 3.6504 on Wednesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7402 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.7477 on Wednesday, and against the mark at 1.9864 shekels after 1.9757 on Wednesday.
In the late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.3635 shekels.
